newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh taka ends firmer on poor dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh taka ends firmer on poor dollar demand.

text.p: A liquidity shortfall in banks helped the Bangladesh taka to gain, finishing at 42.5450/5470 to the dollar in interbank trading, dealers said. This compared with the previous 42.5465/5480.
The taka was quoted steady at 42.5460/5480 per dollar in early trade but gained later as banks were more interested in local currency than the dollar.

Call money was traded at 8.0 to 8.5 percent against previous 7.0-7.75 percent, dealers said. There is a liquidity shortfall after Bangladesh (central) Bank pumped 1.53 billion taka from the market through the sale of treasury bills this week.
